name: Fireflies
description: A night meadow drawn as a blue screenprint, full of 600 tiny yellow-green fireflies, the only warm colour in it, that are dark between flashes, and the beat grid organises them into patches that take turns flashing on the beat, as strongly as the beat is clear. The meadow is a real 3D place seen through one slowly drifting camera: hatched grass receding to a ragged tree line in three paler layers, bare trees with fine branching, mist in the low distance, light grass stalks and seed heads along the bottom edge. Every pixel is one of six blue inks plus near-black, and tone is the density of fine lines and grain; value is depth, darkest near and palest in the sky above the trees. The fireflies fly in that same space, bigger and brighter near the camera, so near and far ones slide past each other as it drifts. Each firefly runs its own clock and flashes when it runs out; a flash nudges every neighbour a little closer to its own flash, 60 ms late, so flashes relay across the meadow in visible sweeps (Nicky Case's Fireflies model, CC0). On a clear beat the meadow is 2 to 4 upright patches, left to right, with waving edges, and each firefly's cycle is as many beats as there are patches (at most 2 s); each beat-grid tick pulls only the next patch's clocks toward the tick and retunes their periods (Ermentrout 1991), scaled by the track's beat clarity, and a flash nudges only neighbours in its own patch. So within about 15 s each patch flashes together on its own beat and the flash walks across the meadow beat by beat: every beat lights a patch, none lights them all. An irregular beat, or one whose clarity is unknown, leaves the swarm free: one meadow, neighbours nudging neighbours, no patches. Every track starts incoherent by design. The world listens only to the slow bass level, averaged over about 4 s: in fuller passages the wind leans the grass and sways the trees harder and the mist drifts faster; it never moves on the beat, which belongs to the fireflies. At near-silence all but 5 % of the fireflies fade out over about 1.5 s, and the meadow stays lit, its wind and mist slower but still moving. Each flash is a light drawn in the print's own terms: a near-white dot with a small, smooth yellow-green halo and a faint four-point starburst, and a short-reach glow that brightens the grass strokes, the mist and the paler branches right around it while the dark between them stays dark (the nearest, near-black trunks stay silhouettes beside a light). The nearest fireflies are soft out-of-focus discs, and trees, branches and grass nearer the camera hide the fireflies behind them, and their light. All of it rises and falls with the flash (40 ms rise, 0.11 s decay), so a patch's flash is many small lights rather than a frame-wide lift. Not certified: the arrow keys reach it, but sessions do not plan it until it is.
author: Matt

audio_routes.note: FF.1 — each beatPhase01 wrap is a grid tick; while K > 0 (FF.5) tick n pulls the clocks of patch n mod P (2–4 patches) toward 0 by K·0.30 of their wrapped error and retunes their periods by K·0.05. At K = 0 there is no pull. K = clamp(2·stems.beatClarity01 − 1, 0, 1), so unknown (0.5) is free (D-257). beatClarity01 and nearSilent01 (the straggler fade) are not declared here: neither is in AudioRoutePrimitives' recordable map, and the committed route_coverage fixtures predate beatClarity01 and never reach near-silence. Both are gated in FirefliesSwarmTests instead.

FF.2 — the world's breath (Matt's "B", D-258 addendum): bassAttRel averaged again over tau = 4 s on the CPU and soft-saturated, 0.5 + 0.5*tanh(4x) (FirefliesWorld.advance). Sets the wind's strength and speed on the grass and the trees and the mist's drift speed, through integrated phases so a change never lurches. Never beat-rate: the beat is the swarm's alone (FA #67).
